profile.name: Zach Schneider
profile.title: Cosmic Code Crusader
profile.about: I'm Zach, a Cloud Developer Principal at GDIT with more than twenty years of building for the web. These days that means Python, R, and React on AWS Lambda, and bringing a cloud-first eye to legacy government systems without losing sight of security or accessibility. Off the clock I build small tools for my homelab, listen to shortwave radio, ride my bike, hang out with my dogs, and drink a lot of coffee.

contact.message: I'm always interested in hearing about new opportunities and projects.

focus: Modernizing legacy federal systems at GDIT: Python, R, and React on AWS Lambda, with security and 508 accessibility built in
Skywatch: copying the Air Force's Emergency Action Messages off shortwave radio with Whisper and help from listeners
Building small Linux tools for my homelab, like motd-forge (Ruby and Node) and updateguard (shell)

projects.name: Skywatch
projects.description: Listens to the US Air Force's HF radio network and copies every Emergency Action Message as it's read, with Whisper doing the first pass and listeners correcting it live.

projects.name: zachschneider.com
projects.description: The blog (code, coffee, cycle), running on zkm-cms: a small CMS built for it with CodeIgniter 4 and Vue 3, whose WordPress importer kept every old URL working.

projects.name: motd-forge
projects.description: A randomized login banner for homelab servers: uptime, disk and memory use, a random quote, and a figlet title. The same tool as a Ruby gem and an npm package.

projects.name: updateguard
projects.description: Snapshots the system before risky OS updates, then checks the machine will still boot before you reboot. Arch and CachyOS, with Debian, Ubuntu, and Fedora in preview.

projects.name: Rustris
projects.description: Tetris in the terminal, written in Rust: 7-bag pieces, wall kicks, a ghost piece, classic scoring, and levels that speed up. No GPU or display server, just a terminal.

projects.name: VVordle
projects.description: A small, readable Wordle clone, written to show how the game works: board state, guess scoring, and an on-screen keyboard, with tests.
